_note: Mockup of the Day 1 Response fight. Numbers come from notes.json (response_combat.scaling): player HP 90, boss HP 85. The deck and the upgrades come from Hardening (the save's deck and equipped_passives); there is no choice here. Each pattern has one upgrade that counters it (counter). With it the pattern plays as written; without it the pattern uses its harsh numbers instead (denser, harder-hitting, or a shorter warning), so a skipped counter costs HP even for a player who dodges well. lockout stops the stream after a number of failed tries, unique stops one hit from opening every account, twostep blocks most of a stolen-password hit, alerts gives a longer warning. A pattern's kind picks how the bullets are made: stream (random heights, one by one, all in one direction), sweep (a wall with a gap that walks through gaps), aimed (a line warns, then a key flies along it; every volley_every shots a fan of volley_count keys). works is the line shown after the pattern when that upgrade did its job; harder (of a defense) is the line shown before a pattern whose counter is not equipped, because then the pattern is played in its harder version: its harsh numbers replace the normal ones (interval, speed, damage, gap, spacing, warning, volley_every, volley_count, spread, box), the box turns red and says HARDER VERSION, and the next-attack preview says (HARDER). say is what the threat says first. box is the size of the arena, lead the seconds a bullet is in sight before it reaches the box. finish is the results screen (FinishScreen): a win pays one reward for defeating the threat; a lost fight shows the same figures and pays nothing. {threat} and {names} (the attacks that got through) are filled into the comments.

comments.flawless: Joshua: Nothing got through. Recovery only needs a final check.
comments.won: Joshua: {threat} is stopped. These got through: {names}. Recovery will repair them.
comments.lost: Joshua: {threat} got through. Check your upgrades and your deck, then try again.

defenses.name: Unique passwords
defenses.works: Only one account was hit. Every other account kept its own password, so the damage stayed small.
defenses.harder: No Unique Passwords: one password opens every account, so the walls are tighter, faster and hit harder.

defenses.name: Two-step sign-in
defenses.works: The stolen password was not enough. The second step (a code) stopped most of each hit.
defenses.harder: No Two-step Sign-in: a stolen password is enough, so keys come in big fans, fast, with little warning.

defenses.name: Lock after failed tries
defenses.works: The account locked after a few wrong tries and the guessing stopped.
defenses.harder: No Lock After Failed Tries: the guesses never stop, and they come much faster.

defenses.name: Unusual sign-in alerts
defenses.works: The alert gave you extra time to react to the stolen password.

patterns.name: Rapid guesses
patterns.teach: The attacker tries password after password, very fast.

patterns.name: One password, many accounts
patterns.teach: One common password is tried on every account.
patterns.say: Summer2024. Let us see who still uses it.

patterns.name: Stolen password
patterns.teach: A leaked password works on the first try. No guessing needed.
patterns.say: No need to guess. I already have your password.

doom.name: NO SECOND STEP
doom.warn: WITHOUT THIS UPGRADE THE ATTACKS CANNOT BE STOPPED: they come as walls with no gap, Dodge does nothing, and every hit takes 30% of your HP.
doom.strike: The thief signs in to more accounts.
doom.lost: Joshua: With only a password, the thief opened every account and the network fell. A password alone is never enough: ask for a second step.

_doom_note: doom: the upgrade this threat cannot be beaten without. When it is not equipped every pattern comes as a wall that fills the whole box (kind doomwall, no gap to dodge through), Dodge cards do nothing, and each hit takes 'percent' of the maximum HP (Block still takes its share). 'warn' is read at the start of the fight and 'lost' is Joshua's comment when the fight is lost.
